newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Ford could make more parts itself.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ford could make more parts itself.

text.p: Ford Motor Co could decide to make more car parts itself and hopes a new three-year deal with the United Auto Workers (UAW) union will prolong the recent record low work stoppages.

Chairman and chief executive officer Alex Trotman said the deal would be a "continuation of the cooperative working relation we have had with the UAW and the workers since the early eighties, almost no lost time, and that has been a major factor in improving our market share, product quality and productivity," he said in an interview with Reuters.
"That's the most important thing in the agreement that we've struck, that we will continue that kind of cooperation," he said.
Trotman said the company wanted to make more parts itself but declined to say what components.

"We're going to run a very competitive company. To the degree that if we think we can be more competitive outside, then we are going to study those things. There are some pieces perhaps we'd rather make inside than buy outside," he said.
"Those kinds of things are the subject of highly confidential studies that are under way and I would not want to speculate what kind of products might come in or go out," he said.
